historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (6.7%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (15.8%): the FY2020 COVID trough flatters EPS growth, and a rising payout (FY2025 dividends US$150m on US$225m NI) holds equity growth down. Revenue 7yr CAGR from FY2018 is only 0.8% -- this is a mature, low-growth OEM whose growth comes from capacity additions.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC (0) - interest income): FY2020 264.1, FY2021 123.2, FY2022 253.0, FY2023 250.8, FY2024 -26.3, FY2025 104.3. The negative FCF CAGRs are a capex and working-capital cycle (FY2024 inventory/receivable build, FY2025-26 capacity capex), not an earnings decline -- net income compounded ~9%/yr over FY2022-25. SBC is zero so reported and owner CAGRs differ only by the interest income strip.

scenario_narratives.base: Crystal keeps compounding as a share-gainer in a consolidating OEM industry: brands keep shifting volume to large, compliant, multi-country suppliers, Fast Retailing stays the anchor customer, and capacity added through Vietnam/Bangladesh satellite factories and the Egypt project lifts revenue ~7% in FY2026 before growth fades toward 2.5%. Productivity gains offset wage inflation so EBITDA margin holds ~14%. Capex peaks in FY2026 then normalises, and owner FCF recovers to ~7% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tariff-driven supply-chain reshuffling favours scaled multi-country producers; Egypt opens EU/US-preferential capacity on schedule, sportswear/outdoor and lifestyle wear (Uniqlo, lululemon-type customers) grow high single digits for several years, and automation lifts EBITDA margin to 15%. Growth stays above 5% through FY2030 and the market pays a slightly higher exit multiple for a proven compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: US tariffs on Vietnam/Bangladesh/Cambodia-origin apparel squeeze brand sourcing budgets and customers push price-downs onto OEMs; Fast Retailing (37% of sales) diversifies suppliers or slows growth, and the FY2026 capacity build lands into weak orders. Revenue stalls after FY2026, wage inflation and under-absorbed new capacity compress EBITDA margin to 12%, Pillar Two minimum tax lifts the cash tax rate to 23%, and terminal growth is only 1.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A net-cash, SBC-free, high-payout apparel OEM valued on owner FCF after a full lease charge and a capex peak. Most of the debate is whether FY2026's record capex is growth that earns its keep or a capacity bet into a tariff-hit demand cycle; the bear weighting carries customer concentration and tariff risk in the flows rather than in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fast Retailing concentration (36.9% of sales): a sourcing shift is a step-change, not a gradual fade.
US tariffs on Southeast/South Asian apparel exports (North America 34% of sales).
Capex payback on the Egypt project and satellite factories; FY2026 capex at a historical high.
Wage inflation in Vietnam/Bangladesh outrunning productivity gains.
Global minimum tax (Pillar Two) eroding tax-holiday benefits in production countries.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 5.47-7.85 HKD
data_sources.fx: Yahoo Finance HKD=X at 2026-10-17T21:00Z; parity-checked against the interim dividend conversion
data_sources.financials: Crystal International annual reports FY2018-FY2025 and interim report H1 FY2026 (research/2232.HK/Extracted); Metrics.csv derived from core_metrics
data_sources.qualitative: H1 FY2026 interim MD&A and outlook; FY2025 annual report directors' report (customer concentration). 2232.HK_Analysis.json bull/bear/risk sections cross-checked after it landed: its ~US$350m planned Egypt investment matches the ~US$340m of above-maintenance capex modelled over FY2026-28.

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,852,822k ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 19); interim note 7 states no potential dilutive ordinary shares. Count unchanged since 2018; no buybacks, no SBC since 2019. Held flat.
inputs.cash_note: Bank balances and cash US$444.365m + short-term bank deposits US$12.265m at 30 June 2026; bank borrowings US$17.753m (all repayable within one year). Lease liabilities (US$29.741m) excluded under lease treatment (B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual cash flow statement: no share-based payment expense since FY2019 (US$0.858m); 2017 award scheme fully vested Nov-2019; 2026 Share Award Scheme adopted but unfunded and no grants (interim report). SBC-zero market; rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.fx_note: Model in USD, per-share values converted to HKD at USD/HKD 7.8479 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-17T21:00Z). Parity check: the interim report converts the HK$513.508m interim dividend to US$65.472m, an implied 7.843 -- within 0.1%, confirming direction (multiply USD by ~7.85 to get HKD). HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows (the group reports and invoices in USD). USD risk-free ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 + ~1.0% blended country premium for a production base in Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China and Sri Lanka -> cost of equity ~10.3%; effectively ungeared (net cash), so WACC 10%. Customer concentration and tariff risk are carried in the bear scenario and its 25% weight, not in an extra WACC premium; same WACC in all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path 0.75% of revenue = principal + interest (FY2025: US$19.3m principal + ~US$1.5m interest = 0.79%; H1 FY2026: US$7.8m + US$1.1m = 0.69%). Lease liabilities excluded from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 PPE depreciation US$60.2m + intangible amortisation US$4.9m = 2.47% of revenue), so cash-tax EBIT is not double-charged.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (US$3.4m stock at 30 June 2026; profit share US$0.02m in H1 FY2026). Flows are consolidated and the NCI stock is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with non-US adaptations (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical apparel OEM). Crystal is the world's largest listed apparel manufacturing OEM (lifestyle wear, sportswear/outdoor, denim, intimates, sweaters) with factories in Vietnam, China, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka and a new Egypt project; fabric costs and freight are largely borne by brand customers, so earnings are processing margins. No prior DCF -- fresh build. EBITDA here is defined consistently with the component build: PBT + finance costs - interest income - share of associates + PPE/RoU depreciation + amortisation = US$360.5m FY2025 (13.65% of revenue), slightly below the Metrics.csv EBITDA (US$377m) whose definition is broader. last_fcf follows the contract formula (reported FCF - SBC - interest income); lease cash (~US$21m/yr) is charged in the forward build via lease_cost_pct_path. Interest income stripped because net cash (US$439m) > 1x the FCF base; the cash pile enters in the bridge. FY2026 capex is guided to a 'historically high level' (H1 US$112m incl. US$30.4m Egypt land; FY2018 peak was US$172m) -- modelled at 7.5% of revenue (~US$212m) then normalising. Working capital is a cash use: inventories + receivables - payables ~13% of revenue, so wc_capture -13% of the revenue change. Not a repurchaser: the flat count is natural (no SBC, no issuance), not funded by buybacks. Dividend policy ~60% payout.
warnings: Customer concentration: largest customer (Fast Retailing/Uniqlo) 36.9% of FY2025 sales, top five 64.2%.
US tariff regime on Vietnam/Bangladesh/Cambodia-origin apparel is the swing factor for North America (33.8% of H1 FY2026 sales).

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +7% (H1 +5.4%, management guides H2 growth to outpace H1 as 6,000 new workers ramp); capacity-led growth decelerating to 2.5%. EBITDA margin edges up from 13.65% on productivity and automation then plateaus. Egypt and satellite-factory capex peaks in FY2026 and normalises to ~1.15x depreciation.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% for single-customer dependency (Fast Retailing 36.9%, top five 64.2%) and an unresolved US tariff regime on its production countries. Base 50% because the FY2026 H1 print and guidance (H2 growth to outpace H1) support it. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right: Egypt execution, tariff-advantaged share gains and sustained margin expansion.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.sanity_check_note: KNOWN BUG (see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug): sanity_check.py historical_table() multiplies the HKD quote price by fx_rate (7.8479, defined reporting->quote i.e. USD*7.8479=HKD) instead of dividing, double-converting an already-HKD price and inflating every historical and implied multiple by roughly fx_rate^2 (~61.6x). Printed implied P/B 14.85x / P/E 106.3x / EV_EBITDA 62.3x and historical P/B avg ~65x are all artifacts of this. Hand-bridged on a consistent USD basis (price HKD7.50 / 7.8479 = US$0.9557): P/E 12.14x, P/B 1.70x, EV/EBITDA 6.35x, P/Sales 1.03x at the current price; at the base-case IV (HK$8.37 -> US$1.0665): P/E 13.54x, P/B 1.89x, EV/EBITDA 7.22x, P/Sales 1.15x. Both are unremarkable for an apparel OEM and consistent with the DCF's own ~10% base-case upside -- a genuine pass, reached via the same backwards arithmetic documented on 0288.HK, 1876.HK and 2099.HK. No driver changes made.
